post.description: Create a sub organization

name.description: The display name of the sub-organization (e.g. 'Acme Corp'). Allows alphanumeric characters, spaces, dashes, and underscores.

slug.description: Optional. The slug of the sub-organization (e.g. 'acme-corp'). If not provided, it is auto-generated from the name. Must be lowercase with hyphens only.

get.description: List of sub organizations

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of sub organizations to return.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The offset to start from. If you enter 10, it will start from the 10th sub organization.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Optional. Filter sub organizations by name (case-insensitive substring match).

parameters.name: orderBy
parameters.description: The field to order sub organizations by. Currently only 'name' is supported.

parameters.name: orderDirection
parameters.description: The direction to order sub organizations. Either 'asc' or 'desc'.

parameters.name: isAccessible
parameters.description: Filter to only return sub organizations that the actor has access to.

patch.description: Update a sub organization

name.description: Optional. The display name of the sub-organization. When only the name is provided (no slug), both name and slug are updated.

slug.description: Optional. The slug of the sub-organization. Can be updated independently when both name and slug are provided.

parameters.name: subOrgId
parameters.description: The id of the sub organization to update.

delete.description: Delete a sub organization

parameters.name: subOrgId
parameters.description: The id of the sub organization to delete.

post.description: Join a sub organization

parameters.name: subOrgId
parameters.description: The id of the sub organization to create a membership in.

projectId.description: The ID of the project to create the proxied service in.

environment.description: The slug of the environment to create the proxied service in.

name.description: The name of the proxied service.

hostPattern.description: One or more comma-separated host patterns the service applies to, e.g. 'api.stripe.com, *.stripe.com'. Each pattern is host[:port][/path]; a '*.' wildcard matches exactly one label.

isEnabled.description: Whether the proxied service is enabled. The agent proxy skips disabled services.

secretKey.description: The key name of the referenced static secret. The secret must live in the same folder as the service. Provide exactly one of secretKey or dynamicSecretName.

dynamicSecretName.description: The name of the referenced dynamic secret. The dynamic secret must live in the same folder as the service; the agent proxy mints a lease and injects a field from its output. Provide exactly one of secretKey or dynamicSecretName. Referenced by name (like secretKey), so a deleted-then-recreated dynamic secret with the same name re-links automatically.

dynamicSecretField.description: For a dynamic secret credential: which lease output field to inject (e.g. 'DB_PASSWORD', 'TOKEN'). Must be a valid output field for the dynamic secret's provider type.

role.description: How the credential is applied: 'header-rewrite' sets an HTTP header on the outbound request; 'credential-substitution' replaces a placeholder value in the request.

headerName.description: For header rewriting: the header to set, e.g. 'Authorization' or 'x-api-key'.

headerPrefix.description: For header rewriting: an optional prefix joined to the secret value with a space, e.g. 'Bearer'.

headerPurpose.description: For HTTP basic auth: 'username' or 'password'. The agent proxy combines the pair into a single 'Authorization: Basic' header. Cannot be combined with headerName or headerPrefix.

placeholderKey.description: For credential substitution: the environment variable name the agent receives.

placeholderValue.description: For credential substitution: the placeholder value the agent proxy swaps for the real secret value on the wire.

substitutionSurfaces.description: For credential substitution: which request surfaces are scanned for the placeholder. Allowed values: 'header', 'path', 'query', 'body'.

credentials.description: The credentials the agent proxy applies to requests matching the host pattern.

get.description: Lists a session's logs newest first, as encrypted chunks of [records](/documentation/platform/agent-vault/session-logs#what-gets-recorded). To decrypt them, follow [Reading session logs through the API](/documentation/platform/agent-vault/session-logs#reading-session-logs-through-the-api). To follow new logs as they arrive, use [the endpoint that tails session logs](/api-reference/endpoints/agent-vault-session-logs/tail). If Infisical can't read the bucket, the request fails with the error `AgentVaultSessionLogStorageUnavailable`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` from the previous response. Leave it out to start from the newest logs.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Return only chunks with records at or after this time. A chunk can also hold earlier records, so filter records by `ts`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Return only chunks with records at or before this time. A chunk can also hold later records, so filter records by `ts`.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: The ID of the session.

isRecordable.description: False if this session's requests can't be recorded.

sessionKey.description: The key that decrypts every chunk in this response, as base64. Null if the response has no chunks.

sessionLogs.description: Whether session logs are on, whether this session can be recorded, and the key that decrypts the chunks.

proxyId.description: The ID of the proxy that uploaded the chunk.

ciphertextBytes.description: The size of the encrypted chunk in bytes.

presignedGetUrl.description: The URL to download the chunk from.

nextCursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` to get older logs. Null when there's nothing older. A page can have no chunks and still have a `nextCursor`.

get.description: Lists chunks added since your last call. Call it every few seconds with the previous `nextCursor`. Any call can return a chunk you already have, so skip any whose `chunkId` and `proxyId` you've read. The chunks decrypt the same way as the ones from [the endpoint that lists session logs](/api-reference/endpoints/agent-vault-session-logs/list). If the AWS connection for session logs can't be used, the request fails with the error `AgentVaultSessionLogStorageUnavailable`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `nextCursor` from your last call. Leave it out on the first call to start from the most recent chunks.

parameters.description: The ID of the session.

proxyId.description: The ID of the proxy that uploaded the chunk.

ciphertextBytes.description: The size of the encrypted chunk in bytes.

presignedGetUrl.description: The URL to download the chunk from.

nextCursor.description: Pass this as `cursor` on your next call, a few seconds later.

get.description: Get all audit logs for an organization

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: Optionally filter logs by project ID. If not provided, logs from the entire organization will be returned.

parameters.name: environment
parameters.description: The environment to filter logs by. If not provided, logs from all environments will be returned. Note that the projectId parameter must also be provided.

parameters.name: actorType
parameters.description: The type of actor to filter audit logs by. Must be provided when the actor parameter targets a non-user actor type (e.g. identity, kmipClient).

parameters.name: secretPath
parameters.description: The path of the secret to query audit logs for. Note that the projectId parameter must also be provided.

parameters.name: secretKey
parameters.description: The key of the secret to query audit logs for. Note that the projectId parameter must also be provided.

parameters.name: eventClass
parameters.description: Filter by event class, comma-separated for multiple values (management, authentication, authorization, data-access). Combined with eventType, only event types in both are returned. If the selected classes include secret events, the environment, secretPath, and secretKey filters drop every event whose metadata doesn't match, including events that aren't about secrets. If they don't, those filters are ignored.

parameters.name: userAgentType
parameters.description: Choose which consuming application to export audit logs for.

parameters.name: eventMetadata
parameters.description: Filter by event metadata key-value pairs. Formatted as `key1=value1,key2=value2`, with comma-separation.

parameters.name: startDate
parameters.description: The date to start the export from.

parameters.name: endDate
parameters.description: The date to end the export at.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The offset to start from. If you enter 10, it will start from the 10th audit log.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The number of audit logs to return.

parameters.name: actor
parameters.description: The ID of a specific actor to filter audit logs by. For user actors this is the userId; for identity actors this is the identityId. When filtering non-user actor types, the actorType parameter must also be provided.

get.description: Get Certificate Authorities

type.description: The type of CA to create.

friendlyName.description: A friendly name for the CA.

commonName.description: The common name (CN) for the CA.

ou.description: The organization unit (OU) for the CA.

country.description: The country name (C) for the CA.

province.description: The state of province name for the CA.

locality.description: The locality name for the CA.

notBefore.description: The date and time when the CA becomes valid in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ format.

notAfter.description: The date and time when the CA expires in YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ format.

maxPathLength.description: The maximum number of intermediate CAs that may follow this CA in the certificate / CA chain. A maxPathLength of -1 implies no path limit on the chain.

keyAlgorithm.description: The type of public key algorithm and size, in bits, of the key pair for the CA; when you create an intermediate CA, you must use a key algorithm supported by the parent CA.

keySource.description: Where the CA's signing key is generated and stored. 'infisical' keeps the key in Infisical's KMS; 'hsm' generates and stores the key in the HSM reached through the specified HSM Connector; 'aws-kms' generates the key in AWS KMS through the specified AWS connection, and every signature is made by AWS KMS.

hsmConnectorId.description: The ID of the HSM Connector to generate and store the CA's signing key in. Required when keySource is 'hsm'.

hsmKeyLabel.description: Deprecated: use externalKeyId, which holds the same key label for HSM-backed CAs. The label of the CA's signing key on the HSM.

appConnectionId.description: The ID of the AWS connection used to create the CA's signing key in AWS KMS and to sign with it. Required when keySource is 'aws-kms'.

appConnectionName.description: The name of the AWS connection the CA's signing key is reached through. Not user-supplied.

hsmConnectorName.description: The name of the HSM Connector the CA's signing key is reached through. Not user-supplied.

region.description: The AWS region the CA's signing key is created in. Required when keySource is 'aws-kms', and returned when reading the CA.

externalKeyId.description: The identifier of the CA's signing key in its key source: the key ARN for AWS KMS, or the key label for HSM. Not user-supplied: the key is created when the CA is created.

crlDistributionPointUrls.description: Additional CRL Distribution Point URLs (HTTP/HTTPS) embedded in every certificate issued by this CA. Up to 4 URLs; the Infisical-managed CRL endpoint is included by default unless disabled.

disableManagedCrlDistributionPointUrl.description: When set to true, the Infisical-managed CRL endpoint URL will not be embedded in certificates issued by this CA. Only custom CRL Distribution Point URLs (if any) will be included.

isOcspEnabled.description: When set to true, certificates issued by this CA carry the Infisical-managed OCSP responder URL in their Authority Information Access extension, and that responder answers revocation status queries for them. Applies to certificates issued after it is enabled.

dnsAppConnectionId.description: The ID of the App Connection to use for creating and managing DNS TXT records required for ACME domain validation. This connection must have permissions to create and delete TXT records in your DNS provider (e.g., Route53) for the ACME challenge process.

provider.description: The DNS provider for the ACME Certificate Authority.

hostedZoneId.description: The hosted zone ID for the ACME Certificate Authority. For Google Cloud DNS, use the managed zone resource name in the format projects/{projectId}/managedZones/{zoneName}.

directoryUrl.description: The directory URL for the ACME Certificate Authority.

accountEmail.description: The email address for the ACME Certificate Authority.

eabKid.description: The External Account Binding (EAB) Key ID for the ACME Certificate Authority. Required if the ACME provider uses EAB.

dnsResolver.description: An optional custom DNS resolver IP address to use for verifying DNS propagation during ACME challenges. Must be a valid IP address (e.g. 8.8.8.8). When not set, the system default DNS resolver is used.

Renew a certificate. The renewed certificate copies the one being renewed, then applies only the changes supplied here. Profile defaults are not applied.

removeRootsFromChain.description: Whether to remove the root certificate from the returned certificate chain.

renewalKeySource.description: How the renewed certificate's key pair is handled. 'new' generates a fresh pair, 'reuse' keeps the current one so the renewed certificate carries the same public key, and 'csr' takes the key from a supplied signing request. Defaults to 'new'.

csr.description: A PEM-encoded certificate signing request to renew from. Its subject, key and extensions take precedence, so only TTL and basic constraints may be set alongside it.

attributes.description: Certificate fields to change on renewal. Anything omitted is copied from the certificate being renewed. Profile defaults are not applied.

allowed.description: Domain component sequences that are permitted. Each entry is one sequence, its components comma-joined most specific first: "corp,example,com" matches DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com. A request matches a sequence only when its components line up position by position, so the same labels in another order do not match.

required.description: Domain component sequences that are required. Each entry is one sequence, its components comma-joined most specific first: "corp,example,com" matches DC=corp,DC=example,DC=com. A request matches a sequence only when its components line up position by position, so the same labels in another order do not match.

denied.description: Domain component sequences that are rejected, each comma-joined most specific first. A sequence is rejected wherever it appears in the chain, so "example,com" rejects DC=example,DC=com and DC=host,DC=example,DC=com alike.

allowed.description: Value patterns this extension may take, with * as a wildcard. Use * on its own to accept any value. Omit to place no allow-list constraint on the value.

required.description: Value patterns this extension must match, with * as a wildcard. Setting any required pattern also makes the extension mandatory on every request.

denied.description: Value patterns this extension must not take, with * as a wildcard. A denied match is rejected even when an allowed pattern also matches.

hsmKeyLabel.description: The label of the certificate's private key on the HSM. Only used when using an existing DigiCert certificate. If more than one private key in the HSM Connector's slot has this label, also set hsmKeyId.

hsmKeyId.description: The hex-encoded PKCS#11 key ID (CKA_ID) of the private key, used to tell apart keys that share a label. Only used with hsmKeyLabel.

caType.description: Optional. The CA type is resolved from caId. If provided, it must match the type of that certificate authority.

reissueFromExternalOrderId.description: DigiCert only. Reissue into this existing DigiCert order instead of placing a new order (reuses the subscription slot). DigiCert revokes the order's previous certificate.

importFromExternalOrderId.description: DigiCert only. Use the certificate already issued in this DigiCert order, without reissuing it. Requires certificate.hsmKeyLabel to point at the certificate's private key on the HSM. The common name, validity and key algorithm come from that certificate, so commonName, certificateTtlDays and keyAlgorithm can't be sent with it.

template.description: Active Directory Certificate Service only. The certificate template this signer requests when issuing (e.g. a code-signing template).

requestedWindowDuration.description: How long the approval stays usable once it is granted, for example '4h'. The window starts when the request is approved.

scope.description: Optional parameters to scope this approval to (command, signingApplication, signingApplicationHash, hostname, osUsername, ipAddress, dataHash). Every value declared here must match at signing time or the sign call is denied; parameters left out are not restricted. A command must match exactly, apart from whitespace, so a different order of options is a different command. ipAddress is compared against the address the sign call arrives from and dataHash against the digest of the submitted payload, so those two hold even if a caller reports something else. A machine identity that declares a scope without naming ipAddress has it filled in with the address the request arrives from; send null to leave signing unrestricted by address.

region.description: The AWS region the CA's signing key is created in. Required when keySource is 'aws-kms', and returned when reading the CA.

externalKeyId.description: The identifier of the CA's signing key in its key source: the key ARN for AWS KMS, or the key label for HSM. Not user-supplied: the key is created when the CA is created.

isOcspEnabled.description: When set to true, certificates issued by this CA carry the Infisical-managed OCSP responder URL in their Authority Information Access extension, and that responder answers revocation status queries for them. Applies to certificates issued after it is enabled.

List all shared secrets created by the authenticated user or identity in their current organization.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: The offset to start listing shared secrets from. Used for pagination.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of shared secrets to return. Max is 100.

post.description: Create a new shared secret that can be accessed by a link.

name.description: An optional name for the shared secret for easier identification.

password.description: An optional password to protect the shared secret. Recipients will need to provide this password to access the secret.

expiresIn.description: The duration after which the shared secret will expire. Accepts formats like '30d', '24h', '1w'. Maximum is 30 days, minimum is 5 minutes.

maxViews.description: The maximum number of times the shared secret can be viewed before it expires. If not provided, unlimited views are allowed.

accessType.description: Determines who can access the shared secret. 'organization' restricts access to users within your organization. 'anyone' allows access to anyone with the link. Defaults to 'organization'.

authorizedEmails.description: An optional array of email addresses to share the secret with. Maximum 100 emails. Organization members in the list get direct access. When allowExternalEmails is enabled, non-member emails are also accepted and recipients will receive the secret link via email, but must use the password to access it.

allowExternalEmails.description: When true, allows sharing with email addresses that do not belong to Infisical. A password is required when this option is enabled. External recipients will receive the secret link via email and must enter the password to access it.

get.description: Returns the full shared secret object without revealing the secret value. Authentication is required for shared secrets that are scoped to an organization.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the shared secret to retrieve.

isPasswordProtected.description: Whether the shared secret is protected by a password.

isAuthorizedUser.description: Whether the current user is an authorized org member. If false, the user must provide a password.

delete.description: Delete a shared secret by its ID.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the shared secret to delete.

post.description: Access a shared secret by its ID. If the secret is password protected, you must provide the password in the request body. Returns the secret value if access is granted, or an error if access is denied. The endpoint requires authentication if the shared secret is scoped to an organization.

password.description: The password for accessing a password-protected shared secret. Only required if the secret is password protected.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The ID of the shared secret to access.

connectionId.description: The updated ID of the Spacelift Connection to use for syncing.

description.description: The updated description of the Spacelift Sync.

environment.description: The updated slug of the project environment to sync secrets from.

secretPath.description: The updated folder path to sync secrets from.

isAutoSyncEnabled.description: Whether secrets should be automatically synced when changes occur at the source location or not.

initialSyncBehavior.description: Specify how Infisical should resolve the initial sync to the Spacelift destination.

keySchema.description: Specify the format to use for structuring secret keys in the Spacelift destination.

disableSecretDeletion.description: Enable this flag to prevent removal of secrets from the Spacelift destination when syncing.

includeAllSubFolders.description: Whether to sync secrets from folders beneath the source path as well.

writeOnly.description: Whether secrets should be marked as secret in Spacelift. Secret values are only available to Runs and Tasks and are not accessible in the web GUI or through the API.

syncOptions.description: Optional parameters to modify how secrets are synced.

contextId.description: The ID of the Spacelift context to sync secrets to.

contextName.description: The name of the Spacelift context to sync secrets to.

configType.description: The type of config element to create in Spacelift. Either 'environment-variable' for individual environment variables or 'file-mount' for a single .env file mount.

mountPath.description: The file path for the mounted file relative to /mnt/workspace/. Required when configType is 'file-mount'. When fileMountFormat is 'secret-per-file', this is the directory path. Example: 'secrets.env' or 'secrets/'.

fileMountFormat.description: The format for file mount config elements. Either 'dot-env' (default) to store all secrets in a single .env file, or 'secret-per-file' to create a separate file mount per secret under the mount path directory.

get.description: List every Secret Validation Rule in the specified project, of any type.

parameters.name: projectId
parameters.description: The ID of the project to list Secret Validation Rules from.

minLength.description: The minimum number of characters the secret key must contain.

maxLength.description: The maximum number of characters the secret key may contain.

regexPattern.description: A regular expression the secret key must match.

requiredPrefix.description: A string the secret key must start with.

requiredSuffix.description: A string the secret key must end with.

keyConstraints.description: Constraints enforced on the secret key when a secret is created or renamed. Omit to leave keys unconstrained.

minLength.description: The minimum number of characters the secret value must contain.

maxLength.description: The maximum number of characters the secret value may contain.

regexPattern.description: A regular expression the secret value must match.

requiredPrefix.description: A string the secret value must start with.

requiredSuffix.description: A string the secret value must end with.

uniqueAcrossLastVersions.description: How many of the secret's own previous versions the new value must differ from. Between 1 and 25. Omit to accept a value the secret has held before.

uniqueWithinScope.description: Set to true to reject a value that another secret in the rule's scope already holds. Requires blind indexing on the project.

valueConstraints.description: Constraints enforced on the secret value when a secret is created or updated. Omit to leave values unconstrained.

providers.description: The dynamic secret providers this rule applies to. A lease is only constrained when its provider is listed here.

minLength.description: The minimum number of characters the generated password must contain.

maxLength.description: The maximum number of characters the generated password may contain.

regexPattern.description: A regular expression the generated password must match.

maxPathLength.description: The maximum number of intermediate CAs that may follow this CA in the certificate / CA chain. A maxPathLength of -1 implies no path limit on the chain.

keyAlgorithm.description: The type of public key algorithm and size, in bits, of the key pair for the CA; when you create an intermediate CA, you must use a key algorithm supported by the parent CA.

keySource.description: Where the CA's signing key is generated and stored. 'infisical' keeps the key in Infisical's KMS; 'hsm' generates and stores the key in the HSM reached through the specified HSM Connector; 'aws-kms' generates the key in AWS KMS through the specified AWS connection, and every signature is made by AWS KMS.

region.description: The AWS region the CA's signing key is created in. Required when keySource is 'aws-kms', and returned when reading the CA.

externalKeyId.description: The identifier of the CA's signing key in its key source: the key ARN for AWS KMS, or the key label for HSM. Not user-supplied: the key is created when the CA is created.

allowedAccountIds.description: The comma-separated list of trusted AWS account IDs that are allowed to authenticate with Infisical.

type.description: How the gateway proves its GCP identity. 'gce' verifies an ID token from the instance metadata server, which covers Compute Engine VMs and GKE workload identity. 'iam' verifies a JWT the service account signed through the IAM Credentials API, for hosts outside Compute Engine.

allowedServiceAccounts.description: The comma-separated list of GCP service account emails that are allowed to authenticate as this gateway.

allowedProjects.description: The comma-separated list of GCP project IDs whose Compute Engine instances are allowed to authenticate as this gateway. Only applies to the 'gce' type, and requires a token carrying Compute Engine instance details.

allowedZones.description: The comma-separated list of GCP zones whose Compute Engine instances are allowed to authenticate as this gateway. Only applies to the 'gce' type, and requires a token carrying Compute Engine instance details.

kubernetesHost.description: The URL of the Kubernetes API server that Infisical reviews the gateway's service account token against (e.g. https://my-cluster.example.com:6443). Omit only when tokenReviewMode is 'gateway', where the reviewing gateway calls its own API server.

caCertificate.description: The PEM-encoded CA certificate that issued the Kubernetes API server's TLS certificate. Required when the API server uses a certificate the system trust store does not recognise, which is the usual case for a cluster CA.

tokenReviewerJwt.description: A long-lived service account token with the system:auth-delegator ClusterRole used to submit TokenReview requests. Omit to have the gateway's own token act as the reviewer. Write-only: never returned by the API.

tokenReviewMode.description: Who performs the TokenReview. 'api' means Infisical does, using the configured token reviewer JWT. 'gateway' means the selected gateway does, using its own in-cluster service account, which requires no Kubernetes host or reviewer token but requires that gateway to run as a pod in the cluster.

gatewayId.description: The gateway to route TokenReview traffic through, for clusters whose API server Infisical cannot reach. Must be a different gateway that is already enrolled and connected. Mutually exclusive with gatewayPoolId.

gatewayPoolId.description: The gateway pool to route TokenReview traffic through. Any healthy member performs the request, so this survives a single gateway going offline. Mutually exclusive with gatewayId.

allowedNamespaces.description: The comma-separated list of Kubernetes namespaces whose service accounts are allowed to authenticate as this gateway. Supports `*` wildcards.

allowedNames.description: The comma-separated list of Kubernetes service account names that are allowed to authenticate as this gateway. Supports `*` wildcards.

allowedAudience.description: The audience the gateway's service account token must carry. Leave empty to skip the audience check.

verifyTlsCertificate.description: Whether to verify the Kubernetes API server's TLS certificate. Verified against the CA certificate when one is configured, otherwise against the system trust store.

authMethod.description: Auth method to configure on the gateway. `aws` carries the AWS allowlists; `gcp` carries the GCP token type and service account/project/zone allowlists; `kubernetes` carries the cluster host and namespace/service account allowlists; `token` is configurationless and requires a separate POST /v3/gateways/:id/token call to mint the bootstrap token.
